newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul braces for violence after police death.
newsitem.headline: Seoul braces for violence after police death.

text.p: Radical South Korean students armed with iron pipes stood guard at barricades at Seoul's Hanyang University on Tuesday after the death of a police officer sparked threats of a crackdown on campus violence.
Prosecutors have called for a round-up of leaders of a pro-Pyongyang student body, some of them holed up on the leafy campus grounds with an arsenal of petrol bombs.

State radio reported that President Kim Young-sam had demanded a thorough investigation into the death of the officer and "severe punishment" for those responsible, depending on the results of an autopsy.

The 21-year-old officer died on Monday evening after thousands of students punched a hole in a police cordon around the university and began lashing out with metal bars at riot officers as they scattered in confusion.
An official at Seoul Police Station said 149 officers were wounded in the clashes.
A student was in hospital on Tuesday recovering from brain surgery after being injured in fierce hand-to-hand combat on a bridge leading to the university.
Students are demanding Kim's resignation, picking up on a popular wave of anger against the head of state over his refusal to reveal his spending in 1992 presidential elections.

Opposition parties insist his campaign spent at least 10 times the legal limit, and was partly bankrolled the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group, whose founder was sent to jail for 15 years on Monday along with top aides to Kim and bank presidents he had bribed.
The leftwing student body, Hanchongryon, on Tuesday expressed regret over the death of the officer, the first fatality in four days of street violence.
But it blamed authorities for the death and defiantly vowed to continue its struggle to bring down the president.
"We pay our condolences to the late police officer, Yoo Ji-woong," a statement said, insisting he had been knocked down by an armoured tear gas launcher. An autopsy was planned on Tuesday.
"We ask that the murderous and corrupt Kim Young-sam regime take full responsibility and resign," the statement said.
"We ask for a fair investigation and warn against using the officer's death as a pretext to crack down on the Hanchongryon," it added.
Kim's ruling New Korea Party condemned Hanchongryon as a threat to democracy.

"Authorities should investigate this incident thoroughly to prevent Hanchongryon's violent uprising from putting down roots in this land. They are a challenge to our free and democratic system," a statement said.

After the last round of leftist-inspired violence at Yonsei University in August last year, authorities arrested 151 leaders of the Hanchonryong, dealing a severe blow to the body that the government says takes its orders from North Korea.
But it has rebounded to take centre stage in the current political crisis surrounding Kim's campaign spending, extracting full advantage from the president's weakness.

Hanchongryon leaders vowed to stage another rally at Hanyang at 2.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Tuesday. They said 1,500 student protesters on the campus would be reinforced by 3,000 others from surrounding colleges.
Squads of riot officers stood across the road from the main campus gates where students had built a ramshackle barricade out of steel filing cabinet, crates and garbage bins.
Teargas still hung in the air, choking students as they streamed into classes. Streets around the campus were littered with rubble and splintered glass from the firebombs.
